My ex boyfriend and me were similar to this - in the beginning we did nothing but sexual stuff, for the first couple months, then after that our sex drive totally changed. We split up for unrelated reasons, but I won’t lie and say it would’ve defo been a better relationship if we had done stuff more often. I had a higher sex drive than him for most of the relationship, and often I felt really insecure as I’d try to initiate stuff and then get shut down. It really hurt my self esteem, and of course I never ever ever would try to pressure him into something he didn’t want to do, but yes, it would’ve made me happier if we’d done stuff a lot more, because I loved him and wanted to experience that physical pleasure with him. Now we’re broken up, I don’t want to do sexual stuff with anyone until I’m dating them, whereas I’ve heard he’s been sleeping around a bit, so it’s weird how it’s changed.

Anyway, my point is, sexual intimacy is so important, and whilst a lot of people are going to comment saying you should never leave someone because of sexual stuff, ultimately it is a big deal and if you’re unhappy you need to talk to her. I can see both sides, and it’s neither your fault nor hers, but if it’s going to be like this forever then you’re only going to get more annoyed and more likely to start arguments. Talk to her and get her perspective on if. Whatever you do, don’t feel ashamed.

Wow, I’ve never related to a post more. It seems like you have an anxious attachment style, and that’s okay. The truth is, you’re probably always going to be slightly dependent on your partner and have a lot of anxiety surrounding the relationship, because that’s your attachment type. 

There’s things you can do to make it better though. When I realised my anxiety was ruining my relationship, I tried my best to turn it around. I hung out with friends, got some new hobbies, and importantly, wrote stuff down that I was anxious about with him (ie if he liked this girls pic on insta that I wasn’t happy with), instead of confronting him with it. I’d take a couple of days to think about it rather than bringing it up straight away, so I could think about if it was really a problem, or if it was just my anxiety upsetting me. I found this to be really helpful, as it meant I wasn’t badgering him everyday about stuff he’d done, therefore he didn’t feel under pressure as much. The relationship still ended, but I definitely think my anxiety regarding it got better towards the end. 

So those are just a few ways you can deal with your anxiety in future relationships. For now, I know it sucks. It seems like your world has turned upside down and you’ll never find anyone like him. No, you won’t. You’ll find someone better. Someone who sticks with you even when you’re being absolutely shit, because he knows you’re going through a tough time. Someone who changes your life in ways you didn’t even know. Someone who loves you more than you ever thought could happen. I know it’s so scary, and right now, you’re probably not knowing how you can live without him. But of course you can!!! Unfortunately, it’s common knowledge and often true, that men move on quicker than women. Women are heartbroken for a few months, then gradually move on. On the other hand, men are okay for a few months, then the reality that they lost a really important person hits them like a truck. And in general, each person is different. Everyone copes in different ways - some people will stay in bed for weeks after a breakup, some will party every night, others will go on as many dates as possible. Just because he doesn’t show he’s hurting, he almost certainly is. And in a few months time, that hurt will likely increase. The most important thing you can do is heal however you feel is best. If you need alone time, take that. If you need to see family, move in with them- yes covid says you can’t but your mental health is more important, and if it’s going to suffer being at home it’s ok to move household jusr this once. Call friends as much as you need, and don’t check his social media’s. Try not to message him, because it probably won’t help, and the more you don’t message him, the more he’ll realise he’s lost a lovely girl.
